note: Key facts a correct lesson should state, misconceptions it must not assert, and a reference page each. Written by hand from standard references; review before relying on them.

keyFacts: A lower gear turns the back wheel less for each turn of the pedals, so each push needs less force.
The same climb then takes more pedal turns, trading distance pedalled for force.
A lower gear means each pedal turn moves the bike a shorter distance, so pedalling takes less force.
The bubbles in boiling water are water vapour (steam), not air.
mustNotAssert: The bubbles in boiling water are made of air.

keyFacts: Water bubbles when it boils because water turns into vapour inside the liquid and the vapour bubbles rise.
A convex lens bends (refracts) light so the image appears larger than the object.
For small swings, a pendulum's period depends on its length and gravity, not on how high it swings.
A compass needle is a magnet that lines up with Earth's magnetic field.
The needle points to magnetic north, which is not exactly the same as geographic north.
Without air resistance, all objects fall with the same acceleration regardless of mass.
mustNotAssert: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones in a vacuum.

keyFacts: Hexagons tile a flat surface with no gaps and use less wax for the area they enclose than circles would.
Sunflower seeds are arranged in spirals because each new seed grows at a fixed angle, close to the golden angle, from the last.
The numbers of spirals on pine cones are usually consecutive Fibonacci numbers, though not always.
Pentagons and hexagons together can make a closed shape close to a sphere, a truncated icosahedron.
Each roll of a fair die is independent, so a six is just as likely after three sixes.
mustNotAssert: After three sixes in a row, a six is less likely on the next roll.

keyFacts: Snowflakes have six arms because water molecules freeze into a hexagonal crystal lattice.
Nautilus shells are logarithmic spirals, but their growth ratio is generally not the golden ratio.
mustNotAssert: A nautilus shell is a golden ratio spiral.

keyFacts: Leaves use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar, releasing oxygen (photosynthesis).
Most of a tree's mass comes from carbon dioxide taken from the air, not from the soil.
mustNotAssert: Most of a tree's wood comes from the soil.

keyFacts: Honey bees find their way home using the position of the sun and landmarks.
Ripening fruit gives off ethylene gas, which makes nearby bananas ripen faster.
Cacti store water in thick stems and lose little water because they have spines instead of broad leaves.
Blood is always red; veins look blue because of how skin scatters and absorbs light.
mustNotAssert: Blood in your veins is blue.

keyFacts: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide.
A candle burns the wax: the wick draws melted wax up, and the wax vapour burns.
mustNotAssert: A candle mainly burns the wick, not the wax.

keyFacts: Ice floats because water expands when it freezes, so ice is less dense than liquid water.
Table salt forms cubic crystals because its sodium and chloride ions are arranged in a cubic lattice.
A cut apple browns because an enzyme reacts with oxygen in the air (enzymatic browning).
Soap bubbles show colours because light reflecting from the two surfaces of the thin film interferes.
A thinner string has less mass per length, so it vibrates faster and sounds higher.
Glassmakers coloured glass by adding metal compounds, such as cobalt for blue and gold for red.
Mixing paints is subtractive, because each pigment absorbs more light; mixing coloured lights is additive.
A bigger drum head vibrates more slowly, so it makes a lower-pitched sound.
Firing clay drives out water and changes its minerals permanently, making it hard; iron compounds change colour.
